Probability is a measure of the likelihood of an event. A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes (heads or tails), making the probability of heads 1 out of 2, or 50%.

C
The die roll and the coin flip are independent events. The outcome of one has no influence on the probability or outcome of the other.

B
Conditional probability is used because the probability of the second event (drawing a red ball) is dependent on the outcome of the first event (drawing a blue ball), which has changed the contents of the bag.

B
Bayes' theorem provides a way to update the probability of a hypothesis (a prior belief) based on new evidence, effectively reversing the direction of conditional probability (e.g., finding P(A|B) when you know P(B|A)).

B
The definition of independent events is that the probability of one event occurring does not affect the probability of the other. Mathematically, this means the conditional probability of A given B, P(A|B), is equal to the regular probability of A, P(A).
